english.title: Adult sexual activity with male child family member aged 13 to 17 - offender over 18 - penetration
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person aged 18 or over whose relation to a boy aged

(A)_[13]_
(B)_[14]_
(C)_[15]_
(D)_[16]_
(E)_[17]_
(F)_[**(..SPECIFY VICTIM'S AGE..)]_

was within section 27 of the Sexual Offences Act 2003, namely **(..SPECIFY THE RELATIONSHIP..), and you knew or could reasonably be expected to have known was of a description falling within that section, and not reasonably believing he was aged 18 or over, intentionally touched him and that touching was sexual involving the penetration of

(G)_[his anus with a part of your body, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PART OF THE BODY..)]_
(H)_[his anus with a thing, namely **(..SPECIFY THE THING..)]_

english.legislation: Contrary to section 25(1)(a)-(d), (e)(i), (4)(a) and (6) of the Sexual Offences Act 2003.

investigatoraction.description: Attracts liability for entry on sex offenders register
Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Provided the victim was under 16 an act done by a person in a country or territory outside the United Kingdom which, constituted an offence under the law in force in that country or territory, and would constitute a sexual offence to which this section applies if it had been done in England and Wales or in Northern Ireland, constitutes that sexual offence under the law of that part of the United Kingdom, and provided that person was on 1st September 1997, or who has since become a British citizen or resident in the United Kingdom he may have proceedings brought against him in the United Kingdom (section 72 and Schedule 2).
(ii) A person convicted of this offence and sentenced to a term of imprisonment of at least 12 months is subject to notification and orders as provided by section 80 of the Act. (Schedule 3, paragraph 26).

other.penalty:
Fourteen years imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
